categories.description: Everything about ticket costs, discounts, and booking options.

questions.question: How much do Aquaverse tickets cost?
questions.answer:
Walk-in gate price is THB 1,595 (~$44 USD) per person. Online advance tickets start from THB 1,176 (~$24 USD), saving you up to ~27%. Children under 3 years old enter free. Online tickets include locker rental (worth THB 300).

View all ticket options and compare prices →

questions.question: How much are children's tickets at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Children under 3 years old enter free. Children aged 3–12 and seniors 65+ may receive a discounted gate price of THB 1,290 (vs THB 1,590 for adults). Online tickets typically use a single price for all ages 3+, starting from THB 1,176.

questions.question: Is it cheaper to buy tickets online or at the gate?
questions.answer:
Online tickets are significantly cheaper. Gate price is THB 1,595 while online prices start from THB 1,176 — that's up to ~27% off. Online tickets also include a free locker rental (worth THB 300) and instant mobile voucher confirmation. We strongly recommend booking online through platforms like Klook or KKday.

Compare online ticket deals →

questions.question: Is locker rental included with Aquaverse tickets?
questions.answer: Locker rental is included free with online advance tickets. If you buy tickets at the gate, locker rental costs an additional THB 300. Lockers are located near the entrance and can be accessed unlimited times throughout the day using your RFID wristband.

questions.question: Are there discounts or promotions for Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
Yes! The best discounts are available through online booking platforms:

  • Klook, KKday, Tiquets: Up to ~27% off gate price
  • Thai nationals: May receive special rates with valid Thai ID
  • Holiday promotions: Special deals during Songkran, New Year, and other holidays
  • Social media: Follow the park's Facebook and Instagram for flash sales

questions.question: Does Aquaverse offer group pricing?
questions.answer: Yes, group pricing is available for parties of 10 or more. Group bookings should be arranged directly through the park's sales team. School groups, corporate outings, and tour operators may receive additional discounts. Contact the park at +66 (0) 33 004 999 for group rate inquiries.

questions.question: How much does a cabana cost at Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
Cabana rental options: Deluxe THB 2,500/day, Super Deluxe THB 3,000/day, and VIP THB 3,500/day. Cabanas include shade, comfortable seating, towels, a personal attendant, and priority food service. Reservations are recommended, especially on weekends.

Read our cabana guide: is it worth it? →

questions.question: Can I get a refund on Aquaverse tickets?
questions.answer: Refund policies depend on where you purchased your tickets. Most online platforms (Klook, KKday) offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before the visit date. Gate-purchased tickets are generally non-refundable. Always check the cancellation policy before booking.

categories.heading: Opening Hours & Schedule
categories.description: When the park is open, when it's closed, and when to visit.

questions.question: What are the opening hours of Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Aquaverse is open daily from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Rides close at 5:45 PM to allow for safe park closure. Last admission is at 3:30 PM. The park is closed every Wednesday for scheduled maintenance.

questions.question: Is Aquaverse closed on Wednesdays?
questions.answer: Yes. Columbia Pictures Aquaverse is closed every Wednesday for scheduled maintenance. This is the most common mistake tourists make — always double-check the day before heading to the park! The park operates normally on all other days (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday through Sunday).

questions.question: What time is last admission at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Last admission is at 3:30 PM. After this time, no new guests are admitted. All rides close at 5:45 PM, and the park gates close at 6:00 PM. We recommend arriving at 10 AM opening to maximize your time — a half-day visit starting at 3:30 PM is very short.

questions.question: Is Aquaverse open on Thai public holidays?
questions.answer: Yes, Aquaverse is generally open on Thai public holidays (except if the holiday falls on a Wednesday). Holiday periods like Songkran, New Year, and school holidays tend to be busier with potentially extended hours. Check the park's official Facebook page or call +66 (0) 33 004 999 for specific holiday schedules.

questions.question: When is the best time to visit Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
For the best experience:

  • Best day: Weekdays (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri) are least crowded
  • Best season: November to April (dry season) has the best weather
  • Best arrival time: 10 AM at gate opening for shortest queues
  • Avoid: Weekends, Thai school holidays, and Songkran week

questions.question: How do I get to Aquaverse from Bangkok?
questions.answer:
Multiple options available:

  • By car: 1.5–2 hours via Motorway Route 7 toward Pattaya (free parking at park)
  • By bus: From Ekkamai Bus Terminal (next to Ekkamai BTS), then taxi from Pattaya
  • By shared van: From Victory Monument or Ekkamai, ~THB 240/person
  • By Grab/taxi: THB 1,200–1,500 + tolls from Bangkok

See complete transportation guide →

questions.question: How do I get to Aquaverse from Pattaya?
questions.answer:
Aquaverse is about 30 minutes south of Pattaya city center in Na Jomtien:

  • By Grab/taxi: THB 300–500 from central Pattaya (20–30 min)
  • By songthaew: Take the Na Jomtien route (cheapest option)
  • Hotel transfer: Some hotels and tour operators arrange transfers for an extra charge — ask your reception

The park address is 888 Moo 8, Sukhumvit Road, Na Jomtien, Sattahip, Chon Buri 20250.

questions.question: Is there a shuttle bus to Aquaverse?
questions.answer: No, Aquaverse does not operate an official shuttle bus. The best option from Pattaya is Grab (THB 300–500, 20–30 minutes). Some hotels and tour operators offer private transfers for an extra charge. You can also take a songthaew to Na Jomtien and then a short Grab ride to the park.

questions.question: Is parking free at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Yes, parking is completely free for all guests. The car park is large with space for cars, vans, and tour buses. Motorcycle parking is also available. The parking area is located directly in front of the main entrance.

questions.question: How do I get to Aquaverse from the airports?
questions.answer:
• From Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK): 1.5–2 hours by car/taxi via Motorway Route 7, approximately THB 1,500–2,000
  • From U-Tapao Airport (UTP): Only 20–30 minutes by car/taxi, approximately THB 300–500. This is the closest airport to Aquaverse
  • From Don Mueang Airport (DMK): 2–2.5 hours by car/taxi, approximately THB 1,800–2,500

categories.heading: What to Bring & Wear
categories.description: Dress code, packing essentials, and prohibited items.

questions.question: What should I wear to Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
Proper swimwear is required for all water attractions:

  • Allowed: Swimsuits, bikinis, board shorts, rash guards, lycra activewear
  • Not allowed on slides: Clothing with buttons, zippers, or metal buckles; denim; loose jewelry
  • Recommended: Water shoes for walking between zones; cover-ups for restaurant areas

All guests must shower before entering water attractions.

Read full dress code guide →

questions.question: Can I bring my own towel to Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Yes, you can and should bring your own towel to save money. Towel rental is available at the park for an additional fee. A quick-dry microfiber towel is ideal as it packs small, dries fast, and takes up minimal locker space.

questions.question: Can I bring food and drinks into Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
No, outside food and beverages are not allowed inside the park. The only exceptions are:

  • Baby food and baby formula
  • Medically necessary dietary items
  • Sealed water bottles

The park has multiple restaurants and snack bars serving Thai and international food at reasonable prices (THB 100–350 per dish).

questions.question: How big are the lockers at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Standard lockers are large enough to fit a backpack, change of clothes, shoes, and personal items. They are located near the main entrance and can be accessed unlimited times throughout the day using your RFID wristband. Locker rental is free with online tickets or THB 300 at the gate.

questions.question: What items are prohibited at Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
The following items are not permitted inside the park:

  • Outside food and drinks (except baby food, sealed water)
  • Glass containers
  • Skateboards, scooters, rollerblades, hoverboards
  • Folding chairs and pop-up tents
  • Inflatable toys and beach balls
  • Sharp objects and weapons
  • Alcohol brought from outside
  • Drones
  • Professional photography/video equipment

GoPros and selfie sticks are not allowed on rides but are fine in walking areas.

See full prohibited items list →

categories.heading: Rides & Attractions
categories.description: Height restrictions, ride details, and what to expect.

questions.question: What are the height restrictions for rides?
questions.answer:
Height restrictions vary by ride:

  • Zombieland rides: 120 cm minimum
  • FlowRider surf simulator: 110 cm minimum
  • Hotel Transylvania kids zone: No height restriction
  • Wave pool & lazy river: No height restriction

Height measurement boards are posted at each ride entrance. Free life jackets are provided for children who don't meet requirements at certain attractions.

View all rides with height requirements →

questions.question: Can I ride alone (single rider) at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Most slides can be ridden solo. Some raft rides require 2–4 riders — in these cases, single riders are grouped with other guests. The FlowRider surf simulator is a solo experience. Check with ride attendants at each attraction for specific requirements.

questions.question: What is the age limit for go-karts at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Height and age restrictions apply for the Bad Boys go-kart experience. Go-karts are an add-on at THB 640 (not included in standard park admission).

questions.question: How difficult is the FlowRider at Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
The FlowRider surf simulator has two modes:

  • Bodyboarding (beginner-friendly): Most guests can do this on their first try. Just lie on the board and enjoy the ride.
  • Stand-up surfing (advanced): Requires balance and practice. Expect to fall a few times! Instructors are available to help.

No prior surfing experience is needed for bodyboarding. Minimum height is 110 cm. Queue times are typically 10–20 minutes.

questions.question: Which zones are best for young kids?
questions.answer:
The best zones for young children are:

  • Hotel Transylvania: SE Asia's largest kids' water playground with 9 kid-friendly slides, splash pads, dozens of water features, and character meet-and-greets
  • Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs: Gentle lazy river suitable for all ages
  • Mega Wave Pool: Shallow areas perfect for toddlers and young swimmers
  • The Emoji Movie: Mini golf and photo ops (dry activities)

Read our complete guide to Aquaverse with kids →

questions.question: Are there any non-water activities at Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
Yes! Aquaverse offers several dry attractions:

  • Bad Boys Go-Karts: Racing track (separate fee)
  • The Emoji Movie Mini Golf: 9-hole themed course
  • Onsen spa area: Japanese-style hot spring relaxation
  • Live shows & entertainment: At the Omnitheatre by the wave pool
  • Character meet-and-greets: Photo ops with movie characters
  • Themed gift shops: Movie merchandise and souvenirs

categories.heading: Food & Dining
categories.description: Restaurant options, dietary requirements, and the payment system.

questions.question: What restaurants are inside Aquaverse?
questions.answer:
Aquaverse has several dining options:

Aquaverse has several themed dining areas. The park uses a credit band system called Foodville for all purchases:

  • Food court: Burgers, grilled meats, Thai dishes, kids' meals. THB 80–350.
  • Thai food stalls: Rice bowls, Thai snacks, fried chicken. THB 80–350.
  • Bar area (Wave Pool area): Smoothies, juices, cocktails, light snacks. THB 80–200.
  • Snack carts & ice cream stands located throughout the park.

Read our food guide with recommendations →

questions.question: Is halal food available at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: While there is no dedicated halal-certified restaurant at Aquaverse, several food options are suitable for Muslim visitors including seafood, grilled chicken, and vegetable dishes. Staff can advise on ingredients. Pork items are clearly marked on menus. For strict halal requirements, consider eating at a halal-certified restaurant before arriving at the park.

questions.question: Are there vegetarian or vegan options?
questions.answer: Yes, vegetarian options are available at most food outlets, including veggie burgers, salads, rice dishes, fresh fruit, and Thai vegetable stir-fries. Vegan options are more limited but available upon request — ask staff for dairy-free and egg-free choices. The bar area offers fresh fruit smoothies and juices that are naturally vegan.

questions.question: How does the RFID payment system work?
questions.answer:
Upon entry, guests receive an RFID wristband that can be loaded with credit at top-up stations throughout the park:

  • Load credit using cash or credit card at kiosks near the entrance and food areas
  • Tap your wristband at all food stalls, shops, and optional activities to pay
  • Any unused balance is refunded at exit kiosks when you leave
  • The wristband also links to the park's automatic ride photo system

No need to carry a wallet around the park!

categories.heading: Facilities & Services
categories.description: WiFi, first aid, accessibility, and other park services.

questions.question: Is there free WiFi at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Yes, free WiFi is available throughout the park. However, speeds can be slow during peak hours with many users connected. For reliable connectivity, consider using your mobile data. We recommend downloading any maps or information you need before entering the park.

questions.question: Is there a first aid station at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Yes, a fully staffed first aid station is located near the main entrance. Trained staff can assist with minor injuries, sunburn, insect bites, heat-related issues, and other medical needs. For emergencies, the park has direct communication with local hospitals. Lifeguards are stationed at all water attractions throughout the park.

questions.question: What happens if I lose something at Aquaverse?
questions.answer: Report lost items to the Lost and Found desk located near the main entrance. Staff regularly collect items found throughout the park. For inquiries after your visit, call +66 (0) 33 004 999. To prevent loss, we strongly recommend using the lockers (free with online tickets) to store valuables rather than carrying them around the park.

questions.question: Is Aquaverse accessible for guests with disabilities?
questions.answer:
Aquaverse provides accessible features including:

  • Accessible pathways and ramps throughout most park areas
  • Accessible restrooms available
  • Wave pool viewing areas, restaurants, shows, and walking-area attractions are all accessible
  • Some water rides may have physical requirements that limit accessibility

Contact the park in advance at +66 (0) 33 004 999 for specific accessibility questions and to arrange any needed assistance.

questions.question: Can I re-enter the park after leaving?
questions.answer: Re-entry is generally not permitted once you exit the park. Make sure to bring everything you need inside. If you need to retrieve something from your car, speak with guest services at the exit — they may be able to arrange temporary re-entry on a case-by-case basis.

questions.question: Is Aquaverse suitable for elderly visitors or seniors?
questions.answer: Yes! Aquaverse is suitable for visitors of all ages. Seniors can enjoy the lazy river, wave pool viewing areas, live shows, restaurants, and shaded rest areas. The park has accessible pathways, and cabana rentals (from THB 2,500) provide a comfortable base with shade and seating. For a complete guide, read our Pattaya Seniors Guide.

questions.question: How does Aquaverse compare to Ramayana Water Park?
questions.answer: Both are excellent water parks in Pattaya but offer different experiences. Aquaverse features Hollywood movie-themed zones (Jumanji, Ghostbusters, Hotel Transylvania) and unique attractions like go-karts and FlowRider surfing. Ramayana is larger with more slides and a natural Thai-garden setting. Aquaverse is better for families with young kids and movie fans; Ramayana suits thrill-seekers wanting maximum slide variety. See our full Aquaverse vs Ramayana comparison.

questions.question: Is Aquaverse the same as Cartoon Network Amazone?
questions.answer: Yes. The park was originally called Cartoon Network Amazone (opened 2014). In 2021, it was rebranded to Columbia Pictures Aquaverse with all-new movie-themed zones based on Sony/Columbia Pictures franchises. The location (Na Jomtien, Sattahip) is the same, but the theming, attractions, and branding are completely different.

questions.question: Can I visit Aquaverse as a solo traveler?
questions.answer: Absolutely! Many visitors enjoy Aquaverse solo. The FlowRider, wave pool, lazy river, and go-karts are all enjoyable alone. Staff are friendly and the park is safe. It's a great way to spend a fun day in Pattaya. Check our Pattaya Solo Travel Guide for more tips.

questions.question: Is Aquaverse good for a couple's date?
questions.answer: Yes! Aquaverse makes for a fun and unique date. Couples love the FlowRider surfing challenge, the relaxing lazy river ride together, go-kart racing, and the themed photo spots. Consider upgrading to a cabana for a more private, romantic experience. See our Pattaya Couples Guide for a full romantic itinerary.

No, outside food and beverages are not allowed (exception: baby food/formula). The park has multiple dining options:

  • Food Court — Burgers, BBQ, and international dishes
  • Thai Food Stalls — Local Thai favourites
  • Snack Bars — Quick bites and chicken dishes
  • Bar Area — Cocktails and drinks

Tip: The park uses a cashless RFID wristband system — load credit and spend without carrying cash.

items.question: Is Aquaverse or Ramayana Water Park better?
items.answer:
Both are excellent, but they offer different experiences:

  • Choose Aquaverse if: You want Hollywood movie theming, variety of activities (water + go-karts + mini golf + onsen), and are visiting with young kids who love the movie characters
  • Choose Ramayana if: You want the biggest water park with the most slides, better value for pure water park fun, and a more relaxing day

Read our detailed comparison guide →

items.question: When is the best time to visit Aquaverse?
items.answer:
Best season: November to April (dry season) for the best weather.

Best day: Weekdays are significantly less crowded than weekends. Avoid Wednesdays (park closed).

Best time: Arrive at 10 AM when the park opens to beat the crowds and maximize your day.

Southeast Asia's Largest Branded Aqua Playground
zones.intro: The Hotel Transylvania zone is paradise for young visitors and families. It is Southeast Asia's largest branded aqua playground, featuring an incredible array of water-based fun designed specifically for children of all ages. The zone is fully themed around the beloved Hotel Transylvania movie franchise, bringing Drac's spooky (but family-friendly) world to life.

attractions.name: 9 Kid-Friendly Water Slides
attractions.desc: Gentle slides designed for children of varying ages and confidence levels

attractions.name: Dozens of Water Features
attractions.desc: Splash pads, water cannons, sprinklers, tipping buckets, and interactive play elements

attractions.name: 2 of Thailand's Largest Water Dump Buckets
attractions.desc: Giant buckets that fill up and dump hundreds of gallons on waiting guests below

attractions.name: Foam Parties
attractions.desc: Scheduled foam parties throughout the day where kids can play in mountains of foam

attractions.name: Character Meet-and-Greets
attractions.desc: Meet Drac, Mavis, Blobby, and other Hotel Transylvania characters for photos and fun

attractions.name: Water Rockets
attractions.desc: Shoot water rockets into the sky and watch them splash back down

zones.tipContent: Parent Tip: This zone has shaded seating areas around the playground where parents can relax while watching their kids play. Arrive early to claim a good spot. For a full family guide, read our Aquaverse with Kids guide.

zones.subtitle: Home to the World's First Water Dome
zones.intro: The Ghostbusters zone is where Aquaverse truly sets itself apart from every other water park in the world. This zone houses the World's First Water Dome, known as the "Proton Stream" — a completely unique water ride concept you cannot experience anywhere else on the planet. The entire zone is designed around the iconic Ghostbusters franchise, complete with the famous Firehouse entrance.

attractions.name: Proton Stream (World's First Water Dome)
attractions.desc: The signature attraction where riders race through dark, twisting tunnels on Ghostbusters floats before plunging into an enclosed dome of water. A one-of-a-kind experience

attractions.name: Ghost Trap Adventure
attractions.desc: Interactive dark ride experience themed around catching ghosts

attractions.name: Slimer Speed Racer Slides
attractions.desc: High-speed water slides themed after the iconic green ghost

attractions.name: Asia's First Ghostbusters Supernatural Water Slide
attractions.desc: A supernatural-themed slide exclusive to this park

attractions.name: Ghostbusters Floats in the Dark
attractions.desc: Ride special Ghostbusters-themed floats through dark tunnels with light effects

attractions.name: Iconic Firehouse Entrance
attractions.desc: Walk through a recreation of the Ghostbusters Firehouse headquarters

zones.tipContent: Must-Do: The Proton Stream Water Dome is the single most unique attraction at Aquaverse and arguably in all of Southeast Asia. Ride it first thing in the morning to avoid longer queues later in the day. Check our visitor tips for the best ride order strategy.

zones.subtitle: Home to Asia's Most Extreme Water Slides
zones.intro: The Zombieland zone is where adrenaline junkies and thrill seekers will find their paradise. This zone is home to "The Beast" — one of Asia's tallest water slides with a heart-stopping 18-meter vertical drop. Themed around the Zombieland movie franchise, the entire zone has an intense, apocalyptic atmosphere designed to get your heart racing before you even step on a slide.

attractions.name: "The Beast" (18-Meter Vertical Drop)
attractions.desc: One of Asia's tallest water slides. Stand on a trapdoor platform, the floor drops out beneath you, and you plunge nearly straight down. Not for the faint of heart

attractions.name: 12-Meter Free-Fall Drop Slide
attractions.desc: A steep body slide that delivers a stomach-dropping free-fall sensation

attractions.name: 360-Degree Spin Slide
attractions.desc: A fully enclosed tube slide that spins riders through a complete 360-degree loop

attractions.name: Body Slide
attractions.desc: A classic high-speed body slide with steep drops and sharp turns

attractions.name: Mat Racer
attractions.desc: Race friends and family side-by-side on multi-lane mat slides

attractions.name: Zombie Chase
attractions.desc: A themed experience where you navigate through a zombie-infested course

zones.tipContent: Height Restriction: Most slides in the Zombieland zone require riders to be at least 120 cm (3'11") tall. The Beast may have additional restrictions. Height is checked at each ride entrance for safety.

zones.subtitle: Enter the Wild Jungle Adventure
zones.intro: Step into the untamed world of Jumanji, where the jungle comes alive with thrilling water rides and immersive theming. The Jumanji zone brings the adventure film franchise to life with lush jungle scenery, roaring water features, and adrenaline-pumping slides. This zone strikes the perfect balance between excitement and accessibility, making it great for teens, adults, and adventurous older kids.

attractions.name: Jaguar Mountain
attractions.desc: The centerpiece ride of the zone. Climb to the top of the jungle mountain and descend through winding slides surrounded by waterfalls and tropical foliage

attractions.name: Viper Slide
attractions.desc: A twisting, turning enclosed tube slide that mimics the movement of a snake through the jungle

attractions.name: Jungle Stampede
attractions.desc: A multi-person raft ride that sends groups hurtling down rapids together

attractions.name: Mandrill Chase Splash Pool
attractions.desc: A splash pool at the bottom where animatronic mandrills "chase" riders into the water

zones.tipContent: Tip: The Jungle Stampede raft ride is best enjoyed with a full group. If you are visiting as a couple or solo, you will likely be paired with other guests to fill the raft, which is part of the fun!

zones.subtitle: FlowRider Surf Simulator with Pro Instruction
zones.intro: Hang ten on the FlowRider surf simulator in the Surf's Up zone! Themed around the animated surfing movie, this zone offers the chance to experience real wave surfing in a completely safe, controlled environment. Whether you are a complete beginner or an experienced surfer, professional instructors are on hand to guide you and help you catch the perfect wave. Note: this attraction requires an additional fee.

attractions.name: 40-Foot FlowRider Double Surf Machine
attractions.desc: A state-of-the-art double surf simulator that generates a continuous wave for stand-up surfing and boogie boarding

attractions.name: Professional Surf Instruction
attractions.desc: Certified instructors will teach you how to balance, catch waves, and ride like a pro

attractions.name: Boogie Boarding
attractions.desc: A great option for beginners who want to ride the waves while lying or kneeling on a board

zones.tipContent: Extra Fee: The FlowRider surf simulator requires an additional fee beyond general admission. Pay at the zone using your RFID wristband. Try to go right when the park opens to avoid longer afternoon queues.

zones.h2: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs Zone
zones.subtitle: Swallow Falls River Adventure & Lazy River
zones.intro: Take a break from the thrills and float along the Swallow Falls River Adventure, Aquaverse's themed lazy river. This gentle, meandering waterway takes you through scenes inspired by the animated film, surrounded by giant food sculptures and the wacky Foodimals from the movie. It is the perfect way to relax, cool down, and recharge between more intense rides.

attractions.name: Swallow Falls River Adventure (335 meters)
attractions.desc: A 335-meter themed lazy river that winds through food-inspired scenery from the movie. Grab a float tube and drift at your own pace

attractions.name: Wacky Foodimals
attractions.desc: Colorful animatronic food-animal hybrids from the movie placed along the river route for photo opportunities

attractions.name: Food-Themed Experiences
attractions.desc: Interactive water features designed to look like oversized food items that spray and splash riders

zones.tipContent: Tip: The lazy river is a great mid-day break. Float tubes are available at the entry point — just grab one and hop in. The circuit takes about 15-20 minutes and you can go around as many times as you like.

zones.subtitle: Miami-Themed Go-Kart Racing Circuit
zones.intro: Step off the water slides and onto the race track at the Bad Boys Race Club. Themed around the action-packed Bad Boys franchise, this zone offers high-speed go-kart racing on a Miami-inspired circuit. This is one of the non-water attractions that makes Aquaverse more than just a water park — it is a full entertainment destination.

attractions.name: 500-Meter Miami-Themed Go-Kart Circuit
attractions.desc: A 500-meter custom-designed racing track with twists, turns, and straightaways inspired by the streets of Miami

attractions.name: Custom Go-Karts (Up to 80 km/h)
attractions.desc: Purpose-built karts reaching speeds up to 80 km/h with adjustable settings for different skill levels

attractions.name: Drift Bikes
attractions.desc: Specialized bikes designed for controlled drifting on a dedicated course

zones.tipContent: Extra Fee: The Bad Boys Race Club is not included in general admission. Go-kart sessions and drift bike rides are charged separately at the venue. You can pay using the credit loaded on your RFID wristband.

zones.subtitle: Creative Mini Golf with Prizes
zones.intro: Take a fun break from the water with a round of mini golf in The Emoji Movie zone. This colorful, emoji-themed mini golf course features creative obstacles and challenges inspired by the world inside your phone. Compete with friends and family for the best score, and top performers can win prizes!

attractions.name: 9-Hole Emoji-Themed Mini Golf Course
attractions.desc: A 9-hole mini golf course with unique obstacles decorated with emoji characters and phone-world theming

attractions.name: Creative Obstacles
attractions.desc: Each hole features different themed challenges that test your putting skills

attractions.name: Prize System
attractions.desc: Score well enough and you can win prizes at the end of your round

zones.tipContent: Extra Fee: Mini golf in The Emoji Movie zone is not included in general admission and requires an additional fee paid at the venue. Great for a dry break when you need a rest from the water.

zones.subtitle: Waves, Films, Concerts & Foam Parties
zones.intro: The Mega Wave Pool Omnitheatre is the beating heart of Aquaverse. This massive wave pool generates mega waves every 20 minutes, and doubles as an outdoor entertainment venue with giant LED screens and Dolby DTS Surround Sound. Throughout the day (and during special evening events), the Omnitheatre hosts outdoor movie screenings, live concerts, and epic foam parties.

attractions.name: Mega Wave Pool
attractions.desc: Enormous pool generating large waves every 20 minutes for body surfing, floating, and splashing

attractions.name: Foam Parties
attractions.desc: Scheduled foam blasts turn the wave pool area into a massive foam party

attractions.name: Outdoor Movie Screenings
attractions.desc: Watch movies on giant LED screens while floating in the wave pool

attractions.name: Live Concerts & DJ Sets
attractions.desc: Regular live music performances and DJ events, especially during weekends and holidays

attractions.name: Dolby DTS Surround Sound
attractions.desc: Professional-grade audio system that delivers cinema-quality sound throughout the venue

attractions.name: Giant LED Screens
attractions.desc: Multiple high-definition LED screens visible from anywhere in the wave pool

zones.tipContent: Tip: The wave pool is the most popular area in the park, especially in the afternoon. Grab your float early and stake out a spot. Check the daily schedule board at the entrance for foam party and movie screening times. Evening events during weekends are particularly spectacular.

extras.heading: Additional Attractions & Services
extras.description: Aquaverse offers much more than just water rides. Relax in the onsen, book a VIP cabana, and capture every moment with the RFID photo system.

items.content:
Unwind in Aquaverse's Japanese-style onsen (hot spring bath) and steam room. After a full day of water slides and wave pools, there is no better way to relax tired muscles and end your visit on a soothing note. The onsen area is separate from the main water park zones and provides a calmer, more tranquil atmosphere.

This is a unique feature that sets Aquaverse apart from other water parks in the region — few water parks offer a genuine onsen experience alongside their thrill rides.

Upgrade your Aquaverse experience with a private VIP cabana. Enjoy a shaded, exclusive area with comfortable seating, storage for your belongings, and dedicated service. Three tiers are available:

  • Deluxe Cabana — THB 2,500/day — Shaded area, seating, locker, towels
  • Super Deluxe Cabana — THB 3,000/day — Larger space, premium seating, drinks included
  • VIP Cabana — THB 3,500/day — The ultimate package with the best location, food & drink credits, priority service

Every guest at Aquaverse receives an RFID wristband that does more than just grant park access. The wristband works as a cashless payment system (load credit to buy food, drinks, and extras without carrying cash) and also connects to the park's automatic photo and video system.

Cameras positioned at key ride moments automatically capture your reactions on slides and attractions. At the end of the day, you can view and purchase all your photos and videos linked to your wristband — a great way to take home memories of your best moments.

For guest safety, certain water slides and attractions at Aquaverse have minimum height requirements. Height is measured and checked at each ride entrance. Key guidelines:

  • Under 100 cm: Hotel Transylvania zone, lazy river, and wave pool (with life jacket)
  • 100-120 cm: Most Jumanji rides, some Ghostbusters slides, Surf's Up (with instructor)
  • 120 cm+: Required for extreme Zombieland slides (The Beast, 360-degree spin, free-fall drop)
  • All ages: Lazy river, wave pool, onsen, mini golf, character meet-and-greets

Life jackets are available free of charge for younger guests and non-swimmers. Read our family guide for detailed age recommendations by zone.

items.question: How many zones does Aquaverse have?
items.answer: Aquaverse has 9 movie-themed zones: Hotel Transylvania (kids), Ghostbusters (thrill), Zombieland (extreme), Jumanji (adventure), Surf's Up (surfing), Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs (lazy river), Bad Boys Race Club (go-karts), The Emoji Movie (mini golf), and the Mega Wave Pool Omnitheatre. Seven zones are water-based and included in general admission. Two zones (go-karts and mini golf) are dry activities with an extra fee.

items.question: What is the scariest ride at Aquaverse?
items.answer: The Beast in the Zombieland zone is the most extreme ride. It features an 18-meter vertical drop where the floor drops out from under you. The zone also has a 12-meter free-fall drop slide and a 360-degree spin slide. All three are reserved for the bravest visitors and require a minimum height of 120 cm.

items.question: Are there height restrictions at Aquaverse?
items.answer:
Yes. Most thrill rides in the Zombieland and Ghostbusters zones require riders to be at least 120 cm tall. The Hotel Transylvania zone is designed for all ages with no height restrictions. Height is clearly posted and checked at each ride entrance. Free life jackets are available for younger guests.

Read our complete family guide for details →

items.question: What attractions cost extra at Aquaverse?
items.answer:
Most attractions are included in general admission. Two zones require an additional fee:

  • Bad Boys Race Club — Go-karts and drift bikes
  • The Emoji Movie — Mini golf

VIP Cabanas are also extra: Deluxe (THB 2,500), Super Deluxe (THB 3,000), and VIP (THB 3,500). The RFID wristband photo/video package can be purchased at the end of your visit.

View all ticket options and pricing →

items.question: What is the World's First Water Dome?
items.answer: The Proton Stream Water Dome in the Ghostbusters zone is a world-first attraction exclusive to Aquaverse. Riders board Ghostbusters-themed floats and race through dark, twisting tunnels with light effects before plunging into an enclosed dome of water. There is nothing else like it at any other water park in the world.

items.question: Does Aquaverse have a lazy river?
items.answer: Yes! The Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs zone features the Swallow Falls River Adventure, a themed lazy river where you float past wacky Foodimals and food-themed scenes from the movie. Float tubes are available at the entry point. One lap takes about 15-20 minutes and you can ride as many times as you want.

items.question: Is a locker included with Aquaverse tickets?
items.answer:
Yes, online advance tickets include a full-day locker rental at no extra cost. If you buy tickets at the gate, locker rental is an additional THB 1,595 per day.

Booking online saves you ~26% off the gate price and includes the locker — it's always worthwhile to buy tickets in advance.

items.question: Are towels provided at Aquaverse?
items.answer:
Towels are not included with standard tickets. You can rent a towel at the park for THB 107 plus a THB 300 refundable deposit (returned when you hand back the towel).

Tip: Towels are not included with any ticket. Bring your own towel to save money, or rent one at the park for THB 107.

items.question: Is swimwear available to buy at Aquaverse?
items.answer:
Yes. Aquaverse has retail shops inside the park where you can purchase swimwear, goggles, sunscreen, waterproof phone cases, and other swim accessories.

However, prices are higher than outside shops, so we recommend bringing your own swimwear to save money.

faqItems.question: How do I get to Aquaverse from Bangkok?
faqItems.answer: You can reach Aquaverse from Bangkok by car (1.5-2 hours via Motorway Route 7), bus from Ekkamai Bus Terminal (2-2.5 hours, THB 108-150), shared van from Victory Monument or Ekkamai (2 hours, THB 240/person), or taxi/Grab (1.5-2 hours, THB 1,200-1,500 plus tolls).

faqItems.question: How much does a taxi from Bangkok to Aquaverse cost?
faqItems.answer: A taxi or Grab ride from Bangkok to Aquaverse costs approximately THB 1,200-1,500 plus motorway tolls of around THB 155. From Suvarnabhumi Airport, expect to pay THB 1,500-2,000. The journey takes 1.5-2 hours depending on traffic.

faqItems.question: Is there parking at Aquaverse?
faqItems.answer: Yes, Aquaverse offers free parking for all guests. The parking area is large, well-lit, and secure. There is no need to reserve a parking spot in advance.

faqItems.question: Does Aquaverse have a shuttle bus service?
faqItems.answer: No, Aquaverse does not operate an official shuttle bus. The best options from Pattaya are Grab (THB 300-500, 20-30 minutes) or a private taxi. Some tour operators and hotels arrange transfers for an extra charge.

faqItems.question: How far is Aquaverse from Pattaya center?
faqItems.answer: Aquaverse is about 20-30 minutes from Pattaya city center by car. A Grab or taxi ride costs THB 300-500. You can also take the white Songthaew (shared truck) on the Na Klua-Sattahip route. There is no official park shuttle bus.

faqItems.question: How do I get to Aquaverse from Suvarnabhumi Airport?
faqItems.answer: From Suvarnabhumi Airport, the drive to Aquaverse takes approximately 90 minutes. A taxi costs THB 1,500-2,000. Alternatively, you can take an airport bus to Pattaya and then a local taxi to the park.

tips.heroSub:
Everything you need to know before visiting Columbia Pictures Aquaverse in Pattaya.
        From what to pack to the best ride order — these insider tips will help you make the most of your day.

tldr.text: Book tickets online to save over 25% — gate price is around THB 1,600, online price starts from around THB 1,200 (check latest prices)
Avoid Wednesdays — the park is closed every Wednesday for maintenance
Arrive at 10 AM opening to hit the big rides first with shorter queues
Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a waterproof phone case, and a change of clothes
Start with Zombieland and Ghostbusters zones first, save the lazy river for the afternoon

tip1.description: A little preparation goes a long way. Here's what to sort out before your visit.

cards.p: Always buy tickets online in advance. The gate price is around THB 1,600, but online tickets start from around THB 1,200 (check latest prices) — that's over 25% off. Online tickets also include a free locker rental (worth THB 300). Most platforms offer free cancellation up to 24 hours before.

Aquaverse is closed every Wednesday for maintenance. Don't plan your visit on a Wednesday! The park operates 10 AM – 6 PM on all other days. Check the official Facebook page for any special closures or holiday hours before you go.

The dry season from November to April offers the best weather for your visit. It's sunny and warm without heavy rain. The rainy season (May–October) can bring afternoon showers, but the park is still enjoyable — and often less crowded.

tip2.description: Pack smart to enjoy your day without any hassles.

cards.p: Proper swimwear is required for all water attractions. Avoid clothing with buttons, zippers, or metal buckles that could damage slides or scratch you.
Reef-safe, water-resistant sunscreen is a must. The Pattaya sun is intense, and you'll be outdoors all day. Reapply every 2 hours, especially after going on water rides.
A small dry bag or waterproof pouch protects your phone, wallet, and room key. You can also rent lockers at the park (free with online tickets).
Bring your own towel to save money. Towel rentals are available at the park but cost extra. A quick-dry microfiber towel is ideal.
You'll want dry clothes for the drive home or dinner after the park. Changing rooms and showers are available near the exit.
While the park uses RFID wristbands for most purchases, having some Thai Baht cash is handy for tipping, nearby restaurants, or the parking area. ATMs are available on-site.

tip3.description: Leave these items at home or in your car — they're not allowed inside the park.

cards.p: No outside food or beverages are allowed inside the park. The only exceptions are baby food, baby formula, and any medically necessary dietary items. Water bottles are allowed but must be sealed.
Inflatable toys, beach balls, footballs, and other sports equipment are not permitted. The park provides tubes and floats where needed on rides and in the wave pool.
Skateboards, rollerblades, scooters, and hoverboards are not allowed due to wet surfaces and safety concerns throughout the park grounds.
Personal folding chairs, pop-up tents, and large umbrellas are prohibited. The park has plenty of shaded seating areas, sun loungers, and cabanas available for rent.

tip4.description: What to wear (and what to avoid) for a comfortable day at the park.
tip4.content:
Allowed

  • ✓ Swimsuits, bikinis, board shorts, rash guards
  • ✓ Water shoes or sport sandals (recommended for walking between zones)
  • ✓ Lycra/spandex activewear
  • ✓ Cover-ups for restaurant areas
  • ✓ Modest swimwear (full-coverage options welcome)

Not Allowed on Slides

  • ✗ Clothing with buttons, zippers, rivets, or metal buckles
  • ✗ Denim jeans or shorts on water slides
  • ✗ Loose jewelry, necklaces, or dangling earrings
  • ✗ GoPro mounts or selfie sticks on rides

Important Rules

  • Mandatory shower: All guests must shower before entering any water attraction
  • Life jackets: Provided free for children and non-swimmers at designated zones
  • Swim diapers: Required for all children who are not toilet trained

tip5.description: When to go for shorter lines, better weather, and a more relaxed experience.

cards.p: Visit on a weekday (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri) to avoid crowds. Weekends and Thai public holidays see significantly more visitors, meaning longer queues at popular slides like the Ghostbusters Water Dome and Zombieland drop.

Be at the gate when it opens at 10:00 AM. The first 1–2 hours have the shortest queues. Head straight to the thrill rides before the crowds build up after lunch. The period from 1–3 PM is typically the busiest.
This is the most common mistake tourists make. Aquaverse is closed every Wednesday for maintenance. Don't show up on a Wednesday — check your calendar before booking transport!

tip6.description: Get the most value from your Aquaverse visit without breaking the bank.

cards.p: The single biggest saving is buying tickets online. Gate price is around THB 1,600, but online platforms like Klook offer tickets from around THB 1,200 (check latest prices). That's up to THB 400+ saved per person. Online tickets also include a free locker (worth THB 300).

Cabanas start at THB 2,500/day and while comfortable, they're not essential. There are plenty of free shaded areas and sun loungers around the park. Bring your own towel and claim a spot early instead.

Load money onto your RFID wristband at the entrance to avoid carrying cash around the park. It works at all food stalls and shops. Any unused balance is refundable at the end of your visit — no waste!

Have a big breakfast at your hotel before arriving. Park food is reasonably priced but adds up. A late breakfast means you can skip the lunch rush, eat a late lunch around 2 PM when restaurants are quieter, and save money.

tip7.description: Where to eat inside Aquaverse — note that outside food is not allowed.

cards.p: The park's main dining area serves burgers, grilled meats, Thai dishes, and kids' meals. The park uses a credit band system called Foodville for all purchases. Prices: THB 80–350 per item. Air-conditioned seating available.
Themed snack bars throughout the park serve fried chicken, wings, rice bowls, and Thai snacks. Casual outdoor seating near the attractions. Prices: THB 80–350. Great for a quick bite between rides.
Poolside bar near the wave pool. Smoothies, fresh juices, cocktails (for adults), and light snacks. Perfect spot to relax in the afternoon. Drinks: THB 80–200.

tip7.reminder: Remember: Outside food and beverages are strictly prohibited. Baby food, baby formula, and medically necessary items are the only exceptions. Sealed water bottles are allowed.

tip8.description: Our recommended route to maximize your time and minimize queueing.
tip8.content:
Morning (10:00 AM – 12:30 PM) — Hit the Thrills

  1. Zombieland — Head here first for the 18-meter extreme drop slide. Queues build fast after 11 AM.
  2. Ghostbusters — The Water Dome and thrill slides are best experienced before crowds arrive.
  3. Jumanji — Jungle-themed rapids and adventure slides. Moderate wait times in the morning.

Midday (12:30 PM – 2:30 PM) — Eat & Explore

  1. Lunch break — Eat at the food court or themed snack bars. Beat the 12 PM rush by eating at 12:30–1:00 PM.
  2. Bad Boys — Go-karts and dry activities. Good to do while digesting lunch.
  3. The Emoji Movie — Mini golf and photo ops. Low-intensity fun for early afternoon.

Afternoon (2:30 PM – 6:00 PM) — Relax & Enjoy

  1. Surf's Up — Try the FlowRider surf simulator. Afternoon queues are typically shorter.
  2. Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs — Lazy river. Perfect for winding down in the afternoon heat.
  3. Mega Wave Pool — End your day here with waves and the Omnitheatre entertainment.

tip9.description: Essential tips for visiting Aquaverse with little ones.

cards.p: This zone is designed for families and young children. It features SE Asia's largest kids' water playground with 9 kid-friendly slides, splash pads, dozens of water features, and character meet-and-greets with Drac, Mavis, and Blobby. Head here first while kids are full of energy.

Some thrill rides have minimum height requirements (Zombieland zone requires 120 cm minimum). Check the height boards at each ride entrance before queueing to avoid disappointment. Hotel Transylvania and the wave pool have no height restrictions.

The park hosts regular foam parties in the Hotel Transylvania zone (usually at 1 PM and 3 PM on weekends). Kids love them! Check the daily schedule board at the entrance for exact times and character appearances.

Baby changing facilities are available in all restrooms. Swim diapers are mandatory for non-toilet-trained children. You can bring baby food and formula — the only exception to the no outside food policy. Free life jackets are provided at water attractions.

tip9.blogLink: Read: Complete Guide to Aquaverse with Kids →

tip10.description: Don't let rain ruin your plans — a water park in the rain can actually be a great experience.

cards.p: You're already getting wet at a water park! Light to moderate rain means shorter queues as many visitors leave. Slides and pools operate normally during light rain. Only lightning and severe thunderstorms cause temporary ride closures.

Pattaya's rainy season (May–October) typically brings afternoon showers lasting 1–2 hours, not all-day rain. Check the weather forecast on the morning of your visit. If rain is predicted, it usually clears up by mid-afternoon.

The park has several covered areas including the food court area, indoor sections of the Hotel Transylvania zone, the Omnitheatre, and covered walkways. The go-kart track and mini golf continue in light rain too.

tip11.description: How to capture the best memories without worrying about your gear.
tip11.content:
📸

RFID Auto-Capture

Your RFID wristband links to the park's automatic photo capture system. Cameras at major ride exits and splash zones take your photo automatically. You can preview and purchase digital packages at kiosks throughout the park or at the exit. No need to bring your camera on rides!

📱

Waterproof Phone Case

A waterproof phone case (IPX8 rated, available at 7-Eleven for THB 100–200) lets you take photos and videos on rides without risking water damage. Test it in a sink before your trip. Alternatively, leave your phone in the locker and rely on the park's RFID photo system.
tip11.proTip: Pro tip: The best photo spots are the Ghostbusters Water Dome entrance, the Jumanji bridge, character meet-and-greets in Hotel Transylvania, and the wave pool sunset view. GoPros and selfie sticks are not allowed on rides but fine in walking areas.

tip12.description: A breakdown of whether renting a private cabana is worth the cost.
tip12.content:
Pros

  • ✓ Private shaded area with comfortable seating
  • ✓ Towels and toiletries included
  • ✓ Secure storage for valuables (separate from lockers)
  • ✓ Dedicated attendant service
  • ✓ Priority food and drink ordering
  • ✓ Great for groups of 4–6 to split costs

Cons

  • ✗ Expensive: starts at THB 2,500/day
  • ✗ Premium locations (wave pool side) cost THB 3,500+
  • ✗ Plenty of free shaded areas available
  • ✗ You'll spend most of your time on rides, not at the cabana
  • ✗ Locker (free with online ticket) stores valuables just fine
tip12.verdict: Our verdict: Skip the cabana unless you're visiting with elderly family members, very young children, or in a group of 4+ willing to split the cost. For most visitors, the free locker and shaded seating areas are perfectly adequate.

tip13.description: Stay safe while having fun at Aquaverse.

cards.p: Always keep children within arm's reach at water attractions, even in shallow areas. Lifeguards are stationed throughout the park, but parental supervision is essential. Free life jackets are available for young children and non-swimmers.

Listen to ride attendant instructions and follow all posted safety signs. Height and weight restrictions exist for your safety. Don't attempt to go down slides head-first or stand up on rides unless instructed.

The Thai heat is intense. Drink water regularly, even if you don't feel thirsty — you won't notice dehydration while surrounded by water. Water refill stations are located throughout the park. Take breaks in shaded areas.

A fully staffed first aid station is located near the main entrance. Staff can help with minor injuries, sunburn, insect bites, and other medical needs. For emergencies, the park has direct contact with local hospitals.

tip14.description: What to do after your Aquaverse adventure — great options nearby.

cards.p: Several seafood restaurants are within a 5–10 minute drive along the Na Jomtien coast road. Rim Talay Seafood and Glass House are popular choices for beachside dinner with sunset views. Expect THB 200–500 per person.

Nong Nooch Tropical Garden is just 10 minutes away from Aquaverse. This world-famous botanical garden features stunning landscaping, cultural shows, and elephant experiences. Open until 6 PM, making it a potential same-day combo.

Jomtien Beach is 20 minutes north of Aquaverse. Arrive by 5:30 PM for spectacular sunset views. Walk along the promenade, grab a coconut from a beach vendor, and enjoy the evening breeze after your water park day.

tip15.description: A few more insider tips to make your visit perfect.
tip15.content:
• WiFi: Free WiFi is available throughout the park, but it can be slow during peak hours. Download maps and info beforehand.
  • Lockers: Free with online tickets. Located near the entrance. Large enough for a backpack. You can access them unlimited times.
  • Parking: Free for all guests. The car park is large and rarely full. Motorcycle parking is also available.
  • Closing time: Rides close at 5:45 PM, but the park stays open until 6:00 PM for shopping, photos, and exiting.
  • Re-entry: Re-entry is generally not permitted once you exit. Make sure to bring everything you need inside.
  • Lost items: Check the lost and found desk near the main entrance. The park also has a phone number for inquiries after your visit.
